data_leaves_device: Measurements go over BLE to the connected client; no RD200 server path is required or specified.
cloud.notes: The newer Ecosense app for EcoQube Flex is not a replacement protocol client for RD200.
cloud.vendor_service: None for RD200 according to the current vendor FAQ

methods.notes: Use both name and GATT shape after connecting. The V1 custom service is not evidence for V2, and an unknown FR: name is not permission to choose the newer command set. Discovery itself sends no commands.

identification.notes: FR:R2 plus the custom 0x1523 service identifies V1. The other listed names plus the standard-base 0x1524 write / 0x1525 notify pair identify V2. The V2 parent service UUID is not established; do not invent it from V1. Unknown FR: prefixes and other RadonEye products are unverified.

device.name: Ecosense / FTLab RadonEye RD200
device.notes:
Mains-powered environmental radon monitor with two incompatible BLE protocol generations. V1 names begin FR:R2 and uses a custom service; known V2 names use the prefixes listed below with standard-base write and notify characteristics. Select a generation from BOTH its advertised name and discovered GATT shape. Never send a command as a generation probe and never reuse V1 configuration/history opcodes on V2.
V1 returns float32 little-endian pCi/L readings inside a command/length envelope. V2 returns uint16 little-endian Bq/m³ readings with different packet lengths and no established V1-style envelope. Convert units with 1 pCi/L = 37 Bq/m³; multiplying Bq/m³ by 0.027 is only a presentation approximation. Preserve raw readings and round only for display.
Only one phone can connect at a time according to the vendor FAQ. Close the vendor app before using another client. This spec covers RD200, not RadonEye Pro, RadonEye Plus, EcoQube or EcoQube Flex.

openness.notes: The GATT and payload layouts are community-recovered. The maintained rd200v2 client covers both generations; radonpy supplies the older framed command and history surface.

upstream_docs.covers: Single-client behavior, no-cloud operation, hourly history and app reset role; no packet layout.
upstream_docs.title: Ecosense — RD200 FAQ

enter_pairing_mode.notes: No application pairing mode or key exchange is used by the inspected clients.

exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app or previous client before reconnecting. No fixed pairing PIN is documented.

pairing.notes: Connect and go, for both generations. Three independent working clients — jdeath/rd200v2 (the Home Assistant custom integration, V1 and V2), lopsided98/radonpy (V1) and ESPHome's radon_eye_ble component — connect, write the read command and take notifications without ever asking the host to pair, and an ESPHome node has no OS stack that would pair behind its back, which is what lifts this to medium. `bonding` is unknown rather than optional because nobody has recorded whether the monitor accepts a bond a phone OS offers. The vendor confirms one active phone connection at a time, so the vendor app holding the monitor is the usual reason it vanishes from a client.

safety_advisory.detail: Do not use a single reading as the sole basis for health conclusions, medical decisions or a safety interlock. Vibration and device status can affect measurement validity, and not all status values are decoded. Follow current local radiation guidance and the manual for the actual unit. Preserve malformed/unavailable values as unknown rather than zero.
safety_advisory.summary: Environmental readings require valid device status and context; a BLE value alone is not a medical or radiation-safety determination.

credentials.notes: No application credential is established. Any OS-level bond is managed by the host Bluetooth stack.

factory_reset.description: Preserve history before using erase_history. Nothing here claims that erasing measurements resets calibration, firmware, bonding or all device settings, and no such full reset is asserted.
factory_reset.effect: No full factory reset or dedicated hardware reset button is documented. The V1 0xE0 command and vendor app's data reset erase stored history; that is a destructive data operation, not a harmless reconnect/reset.

methods.description: Match FR:R2 and the custom service, subscribe to the relevant response characteristic before writing a query, and validate its command and declared payload length.
methods.name: V1 direct measurement and history

steps.action: Close any other connected client, match FR:R2 and discover custom service 00001523-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123.
Enable notifications on 00001525-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 before a normal query, or 00001526-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 before starting history transfer.
Write the selected V1 command to 00001524-1212-efde-1523-785feabcd123 and validate the response envelope before decoding.

methods.description: Match a known newer name and the standard-base write/notify pair, subscribe before each sequential query, and require the exact response length for that query.
methods.name: V2 direct measurement

steps.action: Close any other connected client and discover the standard-base 0x1524 write and 0x1525 notify characteristics; do not guess their parent service UUID.
Write one V2 query byte to 00001524-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, wait for its reply, then stop notifications before the next query.
steps.expect: Measurement 0x50 returns 12 bytes, peak/identity 0x40 returns 68 bytes, and uptime 0x51 returns 16 bytes.

setup.notes: No account, cloud, Wi-Fi provisioning or application key is needed in either inspected client. OS/firmware bonding behavior is not established for every combination, so do not assume a fixed pairing code.

rejoin.notes: Close the previous phone/client and reconnect directly; there is no Wi-Fi network to rejoin.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Two public clients and manuals supply both generations' protocol facts. Upstream tests and mocked GATT exchanges passed on 2026-11-01, but no physical capture was made. The examples below are constructed from the documented layouts, not owner readings or captured device identifiers.

variants.notes: Custom service and command/length responses. A source client's report that newer controllers changed around November 2021 is not a universal manufacturing cutoff; identify by name and GATT instead.
Standard-base 0x1524 write and 0x1525 notify characteristics; exact response lengths and native Bq/m³ integer values. Parent service UUID and history/configuration surfaces remain unknown.

local_access.summary: The vendor says RD200 has no cloud/server dependency; both protocol generations work directly over BLE.

V1_Configuration.description: Payload of V1 response 0xAC: <BBfB = display unit, alarm status, float32 LE threshold, alarm interval.

fields.description: Float32 LE; unit follows current device configuration and must be checked.
fields.name: alarm_threshold

V1_History.description: Start with response 0xE8: first three payload bytes are uint16 LE entry count and a signed byte labeled checksum. Then subscribe to the V1 log characteristic and send 0xE9. Each history entry is two bytes.

fields.description: Signed byte in 0xE8 response payload; source does not verify it and its algorithm is unknown.
fields.name: reported_checksum

fields.description: Uint16 LE divided by 100. Do not label it Bq/m³ or pCi/L without further evidence.
fields.name: history_entry

parse_rules: Accumulate arbitrary notification chunks until entry_count x 2 bytes have arrived; reject truncation rather than padding.
The vendor says measurements are hourly but there is no internal calendar timestamp for a dated series. Preserve order and host-side download/start association.

V1_Measurement.description: Payload of V1 response 0x50: exactly 16 bytes, <fffHH. The characteristic format gives absolute frame offsets.

fields.description: Uint16 LE at payload bytes 14-15; described as previous/10-minute count by the source.
fields.name: previous_pulse_count

parse_rules: Require response command 0x50 and payload length 16, then require all 16 bytes before unpacking.
NaN, infinity and sentinel policy is not established; do not turn non-finite values into numeric readings.

V1_Status.description: Payload of V1 response 0x51: exactly 14 bytes, <BBIIf (16 bytes including command and length).

fields.description: Uint32 LE; the other client interprets it as uptime minutes.
fields.name: process_time

fields.description: Uint32 LE; meaning and electrical conversion unknown.
fields.name: raw_dc

parse_rules: Do not invent status enumerations or an electrical unit for raw_dc. A numeric concentration is not proof of valid measurement status.

V2_Measurement.description: Response to V2 query 0x50: exactly 12 bytes. The first two bytes are an uninterpreted response header, not V1's command/length envelope.
parse_rules: Require exactly 12 bytes. If the length differs, make all five measurement values unavailable rather than decoding a partial packet.
No extra concentration multiplier is applied. Convert Bq/m³ to pCi/L with division by 37 only for presentation.

V2_Peak_Identity.description: Response to V2 query 0x40: exactly 68 bytes. Other bytes and the header are not established.

fields.description: Five UTF-8 bytes at 16-20; handle padding deliberately, do not assume NUL termination.
fields.name: hardware_model_text

parse_rules: Require exactly 68 bytes. Do not publish serial or owner identifiers in logs.

V2_Uptime.description: Response to V2 query 0x51: exactly 16 bytes.

fields.description: Uint32 LE at bytes 4-7. Other fields and any seconds field are not established.
fields.name: uptime

parse_rules: Require exactly 16 bytes. A client may multiply minutes by 60 for elapsed seconds, but must not claim the packet carries seconds.

generation_selection.rule: Match both known local-name prefix and discovered GATT shape; never send a probe command to select a generation.

unit_conversion.warning: 0.027 is an approximate Bq/m³-to-pCi/L display factor, not a wire scale. Preserve raw values and round only for presentation.

v1_framing.checksum: none established for the command envelope; the unverified history-info checksum byte is separate
v1_framing.history_response: arbitrary notification chunks on the separate log characteristic
v1_framing.query: one command byte on the control characteristic

v2_gatt.notes: The parent service UUID was not established, so these characteristics live here rather than in a fabricated services entry. Subscribe before a query, wait for its reply, then stop notifications. The source queries measurement, peak/identity and uptime sequentially, allowing 15 seconds for measurement and 5 seconds for the others; those are client timeouts, not hardware timing requirements. Its ten-minute polling interval is a client policy, not a device requirement.

remaining_unknowns: The V2 parent service UUID and complete response-envelope semantics are unknown. Its characteristic map is in protocol_details rather than a fabricated service.
No V2 history, alarm, unit, clock or erase command is established. Never reuse V1 opcodes on V2.
V1 status/vibration enumerations, raw DC conversion, non-finite/sentinel policy and history-entry concentration unit are unresolved.
The source does not establish the V1 history-info checksum algorithm; do not pretend to validate it.
No universal November 2021 manufacturing cutoff is claimed; select generation by name and GATT shape.
Firmware-update transport, images and recovery are not established.
No physical device was used by this project; mocked/source validation is not hardware confirmation.

erase_history.advanced_reason: Permanently deletes stored measurement history. Download and preserve history first; the documented protocol has no undelete operation.
erase_history.description: Erase stored long-term measurements. This is destructive and is not a factory reset.

read_configuration.description: Query unit, alarm status, float32 threshold and alarm interval; payload layout <BBfB.

read_display_calibration.description: Query display calibration float32. Do not confuse it with a generic concentration multiplier.

read_firmware.description: Query firmware text: first 64 payload bytes, then optional uint32 LE status (absent status becomes zero in the source client).

read_log_info.description: Query history information before transfer. First three response-payload bytes are uint16 LE entry count and a signed byte labeled checksum; trailing bytes are unknown.

read_measurement.description: Query current, one-day and one-month concentrations plus pulse counts; response 0x50 has a 16-byte payload.

read_model_name.description: Query model text; first payload byte is unknown, remaining bytes are text.

read_module_configuration.description: Query <BIIf>: device type, serial date, serial number and float factor. Exact semantics are not established; redact identifiers.

read_oled.description: Query OLED uint32 value. The source client says this does not seem to work; do not rely on it.

read_product_mode.description: Query product/process mode <BBH>: on/off, hour and Bq field; exact semantics are not established.

read_protection.description: Query protection; response command is 0xB3 (not 0xB4), with two uint32 status fields.

read_serial.description: Query serial text; response begins with an eight-character date followed by owner-specific serial data. Redact it.

read_serial_type.description: Query serial type; first three response-payload bytes are decoded as text.

read_status.description: Query status, process time, raw DC value and peak; response 0x51 has a 14-byte payload.

set_alarm.description: Set alarm enabled/status byte, float32 LE threshold and interval byte (1 = 10 minutes, 6 = one hour, 0x24 = six hours). Check threshold units/limits for the actual device first.

set_clock.description: Set six calendar bytes: two-digit year, month, day, hour, minute, second. Persistent calendar semantics remain unresolved.

set_display_unit.description: Set display/reporting unit: 0 pCi/L or 1 Bq/m³. This does not change the documented native V1 float32 unit.

start_log_transfer.description: Start history on the separate log characteristic after subscribing there. Accumulate entry_count x 2 bytes; do not expect one entry per notification.

characteristics.name: V1 control
characteristics.notes: Simple queries are one command byte. Parameterized writes are [command][payload_length][payload]. A normal response uses the same envelope on the measurement characteristic. No checksum is stated by the source clients; validate command and length.

characteristics.name: V1 measurement and command responses
characteristics.notes: Normal response envelope: [command][payload_length][payload]. The format below applies only to response command 0x50, whose complete frame is 18 bytes. Other commands use payload_formats.V1_Status or their command-specific layouts. Require the complete 16-byte measurement payload; one client’s shorter length guard is a bug.

characteristics.name: V1 history stream
characteristics.notes: History does not arrive on the normal response characteristic. Subscribe here before sending 0xE9. Concatenate notification chunks until entry_count x 2 bytes have arrived. Each entry is uint16 LE divided by 100; its concentration unit is unresolved. Preserve relative ordering and explicitly associate download/start times.

services.name: RadonEye V1 custom service
services.notes: V1 only. Do not select this command set for an FR:R2-looking device unless this service is actually present.
